question.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
